title: Shared corpus patterns
description: The cross-cutting shapes every Yomineko entity is built from. Entity schemas $ref these rather than restating them, so a change to what a stable ID or a provenance envelope means happens in one place. This file is HAND-AUTHORED: it was informed by the exported data (scripts/contracts/infer_shapes.py) but the definitions are decisions, and the generated entity schemas point at them precisely so a measurement can never narrow them.

StableId.description: The public, durable address of a record: a lowercase namespace prefix, a colon, then an identifier with no whitespace. Every record in the corpus is addressable this way and the value never changes once published — it is what an API route and a cross-reference both key on. Distinct from the integer `id` some registries also carry, which is a storage row number and is NOT stable across a rebuild. One address is currently SHARED by two entities: a conjugation table is addressed by the vocab entry it inflects (`vocab:1000730` names both the word and its paradigm), so a route that resolves an address has to know which of the two it wants. validate_contracts.py therefore treats conjugation's `slug` as a foreign key into vocab rather than as a declaration; re-keying conjugation as `conj:<jmdict_id>` would remove the ambiguity for good.

IdNamespace.description: Every namespace prefix in use, in two groups. DECLARED — some record on disk owns the address: kanji, vocab, gram(mar), sent(ence), grp (family), read(ing), kana, cap(ability); mod(ule), top(ic), les(son), speak (both a path stage and a unit), course; ex (a lesson's own exercises, declared inside the lesson); cj (conjugation drill), rl (role drill); and the exam sections kr kanji_reading, or orthography, cf context_fill, gf grammar_form, so sentence_order, tg text_grammar, rc reading_comp, pp paraphrase, us usage, plus lt/lp/ls/lr/lg for the five listening sections. REFERENCE-ONLY — no record declares one, they name entries in design/unlock_enums.json: feat (app feature), deck (SRS deck), conj (conjugation form). Nothing $refs this definition, because the pattern that would enforce it lives in StableId and the per-entity namespace is computed from the data into contracts/manifest.json; it is documentation of the address space, and it is kept complete on purpose. Note design/unlock_enums.json calls the family namespace `fam` while every family on disk is `grp:` — the disk is right and the doc's ref_form line is stale.

LocaleText.description: One piece of human-facing prose in every locale it exists in. pt-BR is required because it is the language the course is taught in; `en` is present when the string was derived from an English Layer-A source and is kept for auditing, not for display. Adding a locale is adding a key here — never a new field or a parallel file.

LocaleTextList.description: Like LocaleText, but for a field that is genuinely plural in every locale — a kanji's meanings, a sense's glosses. Kept as a separate definition rather than allowing string-or-array in LocaleText, because a consumer must know from the type alone whether to render one string or join a list.

Level.description: Ordered from first-taught to last. This is DATA, not structure (spec §1.6): the same schema serves N5 through N1, and adding a level is adding rows. Note these are consensus labels, not official JLPT lists (spec §1.5) — see level_confidence and level_sources on any record that claims one. Courseware currently stops at n3; the registries carry n2/n1 rows that no lesson references yet.

Layer.description: Provenance layer (spec §1.1). A = authoritative, straight from an open dataset, zero AI, trustworthy blind. B = derived by AI and then machine-validated against A. C = pedagogy: AI-authored, research-grounded, and never trustworthy without a human teacher's sign-off. A reviewer must be able to audit C selectively and skip A entirely, which is only possible if the layer is recorded per record.

Locale.description: A BCP-47-shaped locale tag: language, optionally a region or script subtag. pt-BR is the only locale authored today, and that is a CONTENT fact, not a structural one — design/i18n.md: adding a language adds content rows, never a schema change. This is a pattern rather than an enum for exactly that reason; the earlier enum ["pt-BR"] contradicted LocaleText two definitions below it.

Provenance.description: Where a record came from and how far it can be trusted. These keys are OPTIONAL and unevenly adopted: most entities carry none of them at the record root (kanji, vocab, family, conjugation, kana, capability, course, topic and the stroke sets do not), `sentence` carries ai_generated/needs_review nested under its own `provenance` object, `lesson` carries needs_review alone, and reading plus the two generated exercise families carry source+layer+needs_review together. contracts/manifest.json lists what each entity actually has. Where a key does appear it means this and nothing else — that uniformity is what is enforced, not the presence.

source.description: The dataset or derivation that produced this record. Free text scoped to its entity (a stroke record says `kanjialive`, an exam item says `sentence+vocab`), because the meaningful vocabulary differs per family.

needs_review.description: A human teacher has not signed this off yet. ALWAYS true for Layer C (spec §1.1). Must be a real boolean: it was once written as 1/0 in four families, and a consumer comparing against `true` read those as reviewed.

ai_generated.description: The content itself was produced by a model rather than selected from a human-written source. Selection beats generation (spec §1.2), so this being false is a quality signal, and every true here should also be needs_review. Formerly spelled `ai` on exam items.

LevelTag.description: A consensus level claim plus the evidence for it. There is no official JLPT vocabulary or kanji list (spec §1.5), so a bare `level` is an assertion; these fields are what makes it auditable. KANJIDIC2's own `jlpt` field is the pre-2010 four-level scale and is never a source here.

level_confidence.description: How strongly the consulted lists agree, as a fraction: 1.0 when every list placed the item at `level`, 0.0 when none did. Derived from level_agreement, never asserted on its own. (Three kanji once carried the word "low" here instead of a number; export_corpus.py now maps word grades to their numeric value, so a consumer can always sort and threshold on this.)

level_agreement.description: The raw tally behind level_confidence, as "agreed/consulted" — "4/4" means all four lists placed the item at this level, "1/3" means one of three did. Kept as text because numerator and denominator are both meaningful and a single float would discard the sample size: "1/1" and "4/4" are both 1.0 but are not equally good evidence. Two sentinels cover the placements we made ourselves rather than read off a list, and they are NOT interchangeable — "0" is an author-added item that appears in no consensus list (confidence 0.0, we are guessing), while "anchor" is a deliberate course placement such as the て-form hub (confidence 1.0, we are certain, there is simply no list to cite). Collapsing them into one value would report editorial certainty as a guess.

LevelSources.description: Which lists were consulted and where each placed the item, as {list_name: level} — three independent lists is the floor (spec §1.5). The KEY SPACE IS OPEN BY DESIGN: consulting one more community list is the operation §1.5 is built around, and it must not be a schema change. Author-added items instead carry {lists: [reason], anchor?: id}, naming why the item is here at all when no list contains it; `note` and `correction` hold the editorial reasoning behind a hand placement. Everything else is a list name and its value is a Level.

lists.description: Why an author-added item is here at all, when no consensus list contains it.

anchor.description: The deliberate course placement this item was anchored to, e.g. `jlpt_anchor:n4`. Pairs with level_agreement "anchor".

correction.description: Why a list's placement was overridden.

IdRef.description: A pointer to another record, by its StableId. The corpus is one graph (spec §1.7): courseware references corpus by ID and never embeds it, so every one of these must resolve. validate_contracts.py checks that they do.

IdRefList.description: A set of cross-references. A field named after an entity (`grammar`, `kanji`, `vocab`) holds references; a count of the same thing is named `*_count` so the two can never be confused by a consumer.
